mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%) signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) indicates a weak labor market and economic slowdown, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which increases corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS increase by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate profit expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines in late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of real GDP (GDPC1 > 13000) indicates a strong economy, which supports positive equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 > 13000.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) signals an ultra-accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% and UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery regimes, a rising CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures that may prompt monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.3% month-over-month in post-shock recovery regimes.
